category_title: Young immigrant boys labeled as 'struggling readers' who exhibit non-normative behavioral engagement (e.g., movement, talk, and gaze aversion) during literacy tasks
minimal_context: The student is working on an interactive reading program at a computer station to read a longer, more complex story.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's start reading this longer story on the computer program.

STUDENT: (Hesitates to read the text. Clicks on a word on the screen to listen to how it is pronounced.)

TUTOR: Try to read the next part on your own.

STUDENT: (Starts trying to sound out the words in unison with the computer voice over, shouting out his responses.)

TUTOR: Please go sit still and read the words quietly to yourself.

STUDENT: Why are you always telling me go sit?! (Continues shouting out his responses loudly instead of reading quietly.)

options.A: Terminate the reading demands and remove the computer program materials for a brief ten seconds.
options.B: Direct the student to stop using the computer program and return to reading physical books.
options.C: Suggest turn-taking between the student and their peer to encourage risk-taking and mutual assistance.
options.D: Tell the student that if they feel angry, they can walk away for a drink.
